title: A poisoned state mutex makes the context-nudge read claim's Drop panic during unwinding, aborting the whole process
outcome: A panic elsewhere while the state mutex is held fails only what it should. The context-nudge worker doesn't turn it into a process abort that also destroys the other tests' results, and tests that assert on the nudge state don't race the background read.
acceptance: With the state mutex poisoned, a context-nudge worker dropping its read claim does not panic during unwinding and does not abort the process; a deterministic test shows this

Every test fixture that asserts context_nudge_in_progress is false after an enable or send is shown not to race the background read, by waiting on its real completion or by not starting it, with no timing-based wait
The owner records whether a poisoned state mutex in production should abort or continue, and why

completion.summary: The context read's claim no longer panics in its Drop on a poisoned state mutex, so one failure can't abort the test process. The live completion fixture waits for the background read before clearing its witnesses. Landed in N10c. Evidence: RED test-e653a6e7 SIGABRT without the fix; master's tree test-b538540d failed at the assertion on Central; N10c pinned test-ad992de5 4/0/0 on Central and test-d6027170 4/0/0 on Linux; FULL test-3236bc1a on DL560. Limits: criterion 2 for engram_host_adapter.rs:97 rests on reading, and neither reviewer read every fixture body behind its callers; it passed in N9's and N10c's FULLs. Other Drops that lock with expect weren't audited. Live proof on a running host wasn't sought; the item concerns tests and an already poisoned mutex. Evidence is standalone or attributed, not registered verification.
